solutionSql: SELECT s.customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id)::integer AS shipments, COUNT(e.id)::integer AS events FROM shipments AS s LEFT JOIN shipment_events AS e ON e.shipment_id = s.id GROUP BY s.customer_id ORDER BY s.customer_id;

rules.howSolved: Grouping over shipments means a customer with no shipment has no group, so it is not listed.
shipments is COUNT(DISTINCT s.id), so the fan-out from joining events does not inflate it.
LEFT JOIN keeps shipments with no event; their e.id is NULL, so COUNT(e.id) adds nothing while the shipment still counts once in shipments.

notes: Read-only item. The fan-out trap is avoided by counting shipments with COUNT(DISTINCT) while events are counted per joined row. Ran without error on sample, nulls and boundary. Solve time is an estimate.
